key_catalyst: Alphabet after-hours slide of 4%+ despite Q2 beat, driven by raised full-year capex guidance to $195-205B sparking AI spending ROI concerns — first Magnificent Seven earnings print of the season turns negative
reasoning: Multiple HIGH-severity catalysts are converging simultaneously: Alphabet's 4%+ after-hours drop on raised capex guidance ($195-205B) is a novel earnings response that introduces a new AI-ROI fear vector not seen in prior sessions, while Tesla's profit decline and negative FCF add a second mega-cap drag. On 7/22, even strongly positive AI earnings (Super Micro +14%, AMD-Anthropic deal) couldn't prevent a -0.51% close because oil above $95 and rising yields were already overpowering stock-specific good news — now the same macro headwinds have worsened (Iran rejecting talks, Houthi Red Sea blockade, 30-year yield above 5.15% for longest stretch since 2007, September hike odds at 83%) while the earnings news has flipped negative, creating a compound risk the pre-market -1.58% may not fully absorb.
